ordered_diagnoses: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma nasal type

s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful lower-extremity swelling and erythema with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful left lower-extremity swelling and erythema
Intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, decreased appetite, and palpitations
Ill-defined, warm, confluent erythema, edema, and tender induration on the left calf
key_facts: 53-year-old Hispanic man
Incidentally noted bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses six months earlier
Denies trauma or injury to the leg
Mild lymphocytopenia, moderate anemia, elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Peripheral-blood flow cytometry was unremarkable
CT and MRI of the leg revealed gastrocnemius myositis, extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema, and popliteal lymphadenopathy
No improvement with intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis
Punch biopsy of skin from the lower leg showed a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells

shortlist.why_kept: Sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells on biopsy, consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Pyomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Gastrocnemius myositis and lack of response to antibiotics, although biopsy did not show typical findings of pyomyositis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and biopsy findings of atypical mononuclear cells, although clinical presentation is not typical for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms, biopsy findings of atypical mononuclear cells, and lack of response to antibiotics, making it a plausible rare diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful lower-extremity swelling, erythema, and the biopsy findings of a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, along with the lack of response to antibiotics and the presence of systemic symptoms such as fevers and night sweats, are more consistent with a diagnosis of Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, which is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that can mimic infectious or inflammatory conditions.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma nasal type
rejected.why: While this is a possibility, the lack of specific nasal involvement and the presence of systemic symptoms and biopsy findings more suggestive of subcutaneous involvement make it less likely.

rejected.label: Pyomyositis
rejected.why: The patient did not respond to antibiotics, and the biopsy did not show evidence of bacterial infection, making pyomyositis less likely.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, but the specific findings in this case are more consistent with the latter diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a type of T-cell lymphoma, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings in this case are more consistent with Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
